sources.title: A Single SNP in an Evolutionary Conserved Region within Intron 86 of the HERC2 Gene Determines Human Blue-Brown Eye Color
sources.access_status: Bibliographic record and headline findings confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; publisher full text not read in this session.
supports: rs12913832 in HERC2 intron 86 as the dominant common determinant of blue versus brown iris colour
Ordinal logistic regression R-squared of 0.68 and association LOD of 444 for this single SNP
The variant lying in a conserved regulatory region controlling OCA2 expression
does_not_establish: That a single locus is sufficient to predict an individual's eye colour
The two-locus phenotype map declared in this work, which is a modelling choice
Any frequency used in this work, which come from the frozen reference panel

sources.title: IrisPlex: A sensitive DNA tool for accurate prediction of blue and brown eye colour in the absence of ancestry information
sources.access_status: Authors, title, journal, volume, issue, pages and PMID confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; publisher full text not read in this session. DOI not independently confirmed and is therefore omitted.
supports: A six-SNP model for blue and brown eye colour
Reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.96 for blue and 0.96 for brown
That a published predictive benchmark for this trait exists and is far stronger than the model built here
does_not_establish: Performance of any model in this repository
Transferability of that accuracy to populations outside the development cohorts
Prediction of intermediate, green or hazel classes, which the cited accuracies do not cover

sources.title: A comparative GWAS of eye colour in light and dark eye genetic backgrounds defined by HERC2 rs12913832 polymorphism in a Canadian cohort of European ancestry
sources.access_status: Authors, title, cohort and the two discordance figures read from the open bioRxiv version of the same work on 2026-09-05; the Scientific Reports page requires authentication and was not read.
supports: CanPath cohort of 5,481 genotyped and self-reported individuals, 2,757 GG and 2,724 AA or AG
33 per cent of rs12913832 GG individuals self-reporting an eye colour other than blue
512 of 2,724 AA or AG individuals reporting a colour other than brown or hazel
does_not_establish: That the same discordance holds in any other population
A causal mechanism for the discordance
The modifier-locus frequency calibrated against it here, which is a calibration and not a measurement

sources.title: Global distribution of the sickle cell gene and geographical confirmation of the malaria hypothesis
sources.access_status: Bibliographic record and headline findings confirmed by web search 2026-09-05; the publisher page redirects to an authentication endpoint and the full text and licence terms were not read. Cited in text only; no figure is reproduced.
supports: An evidence-based geostatistical map of worldwide HbS allele frequency
Geographical coincidence of high HbS frequency with historical malaria endemicity
does_not_establish: Any allele frequency used in a calculation here, which come from the frozen rs334 snapshot
A causal test of heterozygote advantage
Permission to reproduce any figure from that article

sources.title: rs12913832 population genotype and allele counts, 1000GENOMES:phase_3 subset
sources.venue: Ensembl REST API, release 116. Frozen snapshot in data/eye_color_genotypes.csv
sources.access_status: Retrieved live on 2026-09-05, validated against independently supplied allele counts, and frozen with a SHA-256 digest. Offline revalidation is part of the reproduction sequence.
supports: Genotype counts for 2,504 individuals across 26 component populations at rs12913832
The population frequency ordering used to resolve which allele is blue-associated
Exact Hardy-Weinberg testing at this locus
does_not_establish: Any eye-colour observation; the panel is not phenotyped
